subject: Acme pricing estimate & next steps
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Tom O'Neill <tom.oneill@acme.com>, Sarah Li <sarah.li@acme.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-15T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Acme pricing estimate & next steps

Hi Tom / Sarah —

Thanks again for today's call. Quick recap and next steps so we have alignment: 

- Volume profile: you mentioned ~20M tokens/month steady-state with spikes up to ~40M in Q4.
- Primary workload: product search + multi-turn chat for customer support (avg seq len ~150 tokens).
- Budget range you shared: $150k—$250k ARR target for inference spend.
- Target unit economics: you flagged a target cost range of ~$60—$100 / 1M tokens.

Action items from our side:
1) Share a cost model + invoice estimate (attached) that shows on-demand vs committed pricing, and how batching/caching impacts effective $ / 1M tokens.
2) Include an itemized invoice draft for procurement to review.
3) Connect procurement to Monica for billing/PO questions.

I've attached a preliminary pricing spreadsheet (ACME_Redwood_Pricing_Estimate_v2.xlsx) and a short cost breakdown PDF. High-level summary below:

- On-demand (hosted API): est. $95 / 1M tokens.
- 12-mo committed (Dedicated reserve): est. $65 / 1M tokens at 1.5B token commit, includes 99.9% uptime SLA.
- With KV caching / batching on a production access pattern we model an effective $45—$55 / 1M tokens for the most-read flows.

I'll be available tomorrow to walk through the spreadsheet. Monica and Lauren are looped for any billing/ops questions.

Thanks,
Sean
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: ACME_Redwood_Pricing_Estimate_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), token_cost_breakdown.pdf (summary PDF)

Thanks Sean — this looks useful. A couple quick Qs for the spreadsheet before we schedule a follow-up:

- Can you show assumed token mix (prompt vs completion) and how that maps to the effective $/1M? Our product search uses short prompts but long completions for some cases.
- Is the $65/1M committed price inclusive of model updates and rollouts?
- Procurement wants an itemized invoice (line items, tax, billing contact). I've CC'd procurement@acme.com for visibility.

If you can send an invoice draft we can route it to procurement next week. Happy to hop on a call Thursday to review.

-Tom

Tom — thanks for the quick list. I've updated the attached spreadsheet to add a token-mix tab and an itemized invoice draft (ACME_invoice_estimate_draft.pdf). Key notes: 

- Token mix assumptions (prompt:completion = 30% : 70%) are now explicit in the "Token Mix" tab. I've included a sensitivity table that shows effective $/1M tokens across different prompt/completion ratios.
- The $65/1M committed estimate assumes a 12-month 1.5B token commit and includes model update windows (minor version updates). Major architecture changes would be handled via our release/cost policy (we'll note in the contract).
- Line items included: monthly committed fee, overage rate (per 1M tokens), optional premium support + SLA surcharge. Taxes not included — we'll surface those on the formal invoice.

Attached: ACME_Redwood_Pricing_Estimate_v2.xlsx, token_cost_breakdown.pdf, ACME_invoice_estimate_draft.pdf

Looping Monica for billing confirmation.

Best,
Sean
